label: Cog Sinister / Gonzo
release_notes: Billed as the band's final studio album. Nine tracks built from unused Mark E. Smith vocal and lyric recordings made between 2001 and 2014, set to new backing tracks. Three vocals are by Ed Blaney and a couple by Simon "Ding" Archer (Louder Than War).

Assembled by Smith confidants Ed Blaney (friend, solo artist) and Simon "Ding" Archer (former Fall bassist, long-time Fall engineer at 6DB studio; credits include PJ Harvey and Pixies). Cog Sinister / Gonzo, cat. COGGZ154 (LP, CD).

Backing tracks run to industrial and metallic noise rather than the band's late-period garage sound (Louder Than War). Reviewers split on the Fall name: Progressive Aspect calls it "Fall by numbers" and finds Smith's vocals largely impenetrable, and Real Gone notes repeated cut-up vocals.

Disputed release: Smith's fiancee and last manager Pamela Vander called it ethically wrong and says Smith named New Facts Emerge (2017) as the final album. Dork reports the album has the approval of Smith's estate. Reports conflict, so flag this if you mention it on air.
Release date conflict: Wikipedia and Album of the Year list Oct. 2, 2026. Louder Than War lists Sept. 8. Nine tracks, about 44 minutes.

pull_quotes.text: grinding, metallic slabs of industrial noise that stand up in their own right

draft_comment: Posthumous Fall: unused Mark E. Smith vocals from 2001 to 2014, set to new industrial-leaning backing tracks by Ed Blaney and Simon Archer. Contested, loud and short on warmth. One more Fall album, with asterisks.

tracks.title: 30 Degrees
tracks.notes: Lead single (June 12, 2026). Written by Smith with Archer and Blaney.

tracks.title: So Long
tracks.notes: Named as a highlight by Maximum Volume Music.

tracks.title: Colonel's Retreat
tracks.notes: Sleeve spells it Colonels Retreat. Maximum Volume Music says it and A Caveat deepen the album's atmosphere. Progressive Aspect says the pair blur together.

tracks.title: A Caveat
tracks.notes: See Colonel's Retreat: same split in reviews (Maximum Volume Music, Progressive Aspect).

tracks.title: Final Position
tracks.notes: Real Gone groups it with Irish Northern Man as material some fans may reject.

tracks.title: Retro Song
tracks.notes: Most praised track in reviews (Maximum Volume Music calls it possibly the album's funniest idea). Described as the most energetic song on the record.

tracks.title: Irish Northern Man
tracks.notes: Over 7 minutes. One review describes eerie backing under snarling, growling Smith vocals. Long, so plan a fade or a short intro.

tracks.title: The Book
tracks.notes: Closer. Longest of the last three tracks at 6:23.
